# Expenses & Getting Paid – FAQs

For the steps from planning a purchase to payment, start with the [expense guide](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/). This page answers specific payment questions.

## How does paying people work?

Submit an expense through the Collective’s page. Expenses are reviewed by the Collective and OSE. If the sole administrator requests their own reimbursement, OSE can check the supporting documents and pay without a second approver on the Collective side.

We aim to initiate payment within seven business days once the expense is complete and approved and the necessary funds have been received and are available. Bank processing time is additional. This is a target, not a guaranteed date of receipt.

***

## How do I get paid / reimbursed / receive my grant money?

Go to your initiative's page and click **“Submit Expense”**. You’ll need to log in (or create an account), then upload a valid receipt or invoice.

> **Note:** [How to submit an expense – Open Collective Docs](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/submitting-expenses)

***

## Invoice or Reimbursement – which one do I need?

* **Reimbursement**: Use this when you've paid out-of-pocket. A receipt is required (must include vendor name, address, and tax ID). Order confirmations are not valid receipts.
* **Invoice**: Use this when you're requesting payment for services. A formal invoice is required, including contact details, tax info, and description of services.

> **Note:** [Invoices vs. Reimbursements – OSE Docs](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/)

***

## Can we pay people for their time?

Collectives can pay service providers against a compliant invoice, including through a workers’ cooperative. Agree the work, price and dates with the Collective and submit the invoice through Open Collective for review. OSE does not provide a standard employment or payroll service. Any arrangement requiring OSE to sign a specific contract must be discussed and accepted beforehand.

## Which documents are needed?

Invoices must be addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number to have invoices issued.

Reimbursements require an invoice or receipt. A bank statement alone is insufficient. See the [expense guide](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/) and [Invoices or Reimbursements?](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/).

***

## Can I donate part of my Collective’s budget to a charity?

Ordinary external donations may be made to identified nonprofit organisations after OSE has reviewed and approved the beneficiary, purpose and funding conditions. Contact OSE before committing or requesting payment. Other recipient types require a specific assessment, without any promise of acceptance. Once OSE has confirmed the arrangement, the beneficiary submits the request with the following documents:

* A donation request letter signed by one of their administrators, stating the amount and purpose of the donation
* Their incorporation document
* Their bank identification details

> **Danger:** A donation is distinct from payment for goods or services. It may still carry restrictions on use and reporting obligations. If a benefit or service is promised in return, discuss the arrangement with OSE before proceeding.

***

## Are receipts and invoices public?

Only general information (amount, description, purpose) is public. Uploaded documents (invoices, receipts) are private — visible only to the Collective’s admins and OSE staff.

***

## Need help?

Use the comments on the expense for routine questions and follow-up. For sensitive information, contact OSE privately at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Expenses

Prepare a payment from your Collective's budget. Start by choosing the situation that matches your request.

## Choose your payment

| Your situation                                             | Where to start                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| You have already paid for something for the Collective     | [Prepare a reimbursement](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/#prepare-a-reimbursement)      |
| A supplier needs to be paid for goods or services          | [Prepare an invoice](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/#prepare-an-invoice)                |
| The payment is a donation or grant to another organisation | [Ask OSE about an outgoing grant or donation](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only/) |

## Before you submit

* Have the invoice or receipt and the details needed for payment ready. A bank statement alone is insufficient for reimbursement.
* Check that the necessary funds have been received and are available.
* For supplier invoices, use the Collective's name or the person who placed the order; do not use OSE's legal name or VAT number.
* If eligibility is unclear, ask OSE before spending. A specific contract signed by OSE requires advance agreement.

**Ready?** Go to Submission Process. **Already submitted?** Read Approval Workflow, or use the expense comments for routine follow-up. Send sensitive information privately.

**Payment target:** seven business days once the expense is complete and approved and funds are available; bank processing time is additional. This is not a guaranteed receipt date.

## Overview

Managing expenses with Open Source Europe (OSE) is designed to be transparent and straightforward. Whether you're reimbursing a team member or paying a service provider, the process ensures accountability and compliance with fiscal regulations.

***

## Before spending and requesting reimbursement

OSE does not require systematic advance approval for ordinary expenses. If eligibility is unclear, contact the team before spending. Reimbursement remains subject to review. Any arrangement requiring a specific contract signed by OSE must be discussed and accepted in advance.

If someone cannot advance the cost, direct payment to the supplier on a compliant invoice is possible. OSE does not provide advances to individuals.

***

## Types of Expenses

There are two primary types of expenses you can submit:

### 1. **Reimbursements**

Used when someone has paid out-of-pocket for goods or services on behalf of the Collective.

* **Required Documentation**: **Fiscal receipts**
  * Vendor's name, address and tax reference
  * Transaction date
  * Description of items or services
  * Amount paid

> **Note**: Order confirmations, proforma invoices, or bank statements are not valid receipts. Learn more: [How to Submit a Reimbursement](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/reimbursement)

### 2. **Invoices**

Used when paying individuals or organizations for services rendered.

* **Required Documentation**:
  * Unique invoice number
  * Service provider's full details (name, address, tax ID)
  * Detailed description of services
  * Applicable tax rate and amount
  * Invoice addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order

> **Important**: Invoices must be addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number to have invoices issued. Learn more: [How to Submit an Invoice](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/invoices)

***

## Supporting documents and timing of submission

Without an invoice or receipt, OSE refuses reimbursement; a bank statement alone is insufficient. For durable equipment, the usual supporting documents are required; OSE does not systematically require an additional inventory. Specific funding or agreement requirements still apply.

There is no general fixed deadline for submitting a reimbursement, but deadlines attached to a funding agreement or closure must be respected. Expenses incurred before the Collective was accepted by OSE may be reimbursed after review of their connection to the project, documents and funding conditions, provided funds are available.

***

## Paying service providers

Collectives can pay service providers against a compliant invoice, including through a workers’ cooperative. Agree the work, price and dates with the Collective and submit the invoice through Open Collective for review. OSE does not provide a standard employment or payroll service. Any arrangement requiring OSE to sign a specific contract must be discussed and accepted beforehand.

***

## Submission Process

1. Go to your Collective's page and click **“Submit Expense”**
2. Choose the expense type: **Reimbursement** or **Invoice**
3. Fill in the required details and upload documentation
4. Select a payout method (e.g., PayPal, Wise/bank transfer)
5. Submit for approval

> **Processing Time**: We aim to initiate payment within seven business days once the expense is complete and approved and the necessary funds have been received and are available. Bank processing time is additional. This is a target, not a guaranteed date of receipt.

***

## Approval Workflow

Expenses are reviewed by the Collective and OSE. If the sole administrator requests their own reimbursement, OSE can check the supporting documents and pay without a second approver on the Collective side.

OSE checks the documents before payment. Incomplete or non-compliant expenses may be rejected. A promised donation or grant is not an available balance: funds must be received and available before payment.

***

## Payment Methods

Supported payout options:

* **PayPal** (must be active and verified)
* **Bank Transfer via Wise** (international bank details required)

> **Caution**: Ensure that payout details match the expense documentation to avoid delays.

***

## Compliance and Best Practices

* **Transparency**: All expenses are publicly visible to ensure accountability.
* **Accuracy**: Double-check amounts, details, and receipts before submitting.
* **Communication**: Use expense comments for routine questions and follow-up. Contact OSE privately for sensitive information; do not put sensitive documents or bank details in comments.

> **Need help?** Email us at <home@opensourceeurope.org>

***

## Learn More

* [Overview: How to Submit Expenses](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/submitting-expenses)
* [Expenses in the Ledger – Open Collective Docs](https://docs.opencollective.com/open-collective-docs/product/ledger/expenses-in-the-ledger)
* [Expenses and getting paid: frequently asked questions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/expenses-and-getting-paid-faqs/)
* [Outgoing grants and donations](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only/)


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Invoices or Reimbursements?

Choose the request type before submitting an expense. Use **Reimbursement** if you have already paid; use **Invoice** when a supplier is requesting payment for goods or services.

## Submit your request

1. Choose the matching document checklist below: **Invoice** or **Reimbursement**.
2. Open your Collective on Open Collective and choose **Submit Expense**.
3. Select the type, complete the details, attach the supporting document and choose the payout method.
4. Submit for Collective and OSE review. Follow the [approval and payment guidance](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/#approval-workflow).

**Someone cannot advance the cost?** Direct payment to the supplier on a compliant invoice is possible. OSE does not provide advances to individuals. Payment is subject to review and available funds.

For a donation or grant to another organisation, use the [outgoing grants guide](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only/) instead of treating it as a supplier invoice.

## Understanding the Difference

When submitting expenses to your Collective, it's essential to choose the correct type:

## Prepare an invoice

### 1. **Invoice**

Use this when you're requesting payment for services rendered or goods provided.

* **Who submits**: Freelancers, contractors, or companies
* **Purpose**: Payment for work completed or goods delivered
* **Documentation**: A formal invoice containing:
  * Unique invoice number
  * Full identification (name, address, tax/company number)
  * Detailed description of the service or goods
  * Applicable tax rate and amount. If the tax rate is zero, please provide a legal reference for the exemption directly on the invoice (e.g., VAT exemption according to the article YY of the law XX).
  * Invoice addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order, with the appropriate recipient details

> **Important**: Invoices must be addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number to have invoices issued.

***

## Prepare a reimbursement

### 2. **Reimbursement**

Use this when you've paid out-of-pocket on behalf of the Collective and seek reimbursement.

* **Who submits**: Members or contributors of the Collective
* **Purpose**: Reimbursement for purchases made for the Collective
* **Documentation**: A valid receipt from the provider showing:
  * Vendor's name and address
  * Transaction date
  * Description of items or services
  * Amount paid

> **Note:** Order confirmations, proforma invoices, bank or PayPal statements are not valid receipts.

***

## Special Cases

* **Partial Reimbursements**: If you're requesting reimbursement for only part of a receipt, highlight the relevant items directly on the document.

> **Tip:** If the breakdown isn’t obvious (e.g., a percentage or a split), please attach a signed and dated note explaining the amount being claimed and what it covers.

***

## Learn More

For more detailed explanations and tutorials, refer to:

* [Overview: Submitting Expenses](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/submitting-expenses)
* [Expenses: General Guidance](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/collectives/expenses)

***

## Need Help?

If you have any questions, feel free to [contact us](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org). We're happy to help.

## Documents and review

Without an invoice or receipt, reimbursement is refused. A bank statement alone is insufficient. See [Expenses](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/) for the rules on prior spending, submission timing, available funds and payment targets.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Request a Grant (for Nonprofits Only)

In addition to submitting an expense or invoice, the Open Collective platform also includes the option to “Request a Grant.”

Collectives may also request approval for donations to identified nonprofit organisations. That permission is distinct from access to the specific “Request a Grant” feature described below. OSE reviews the beneficiary, purpose and funding conditions before accepting an outgoing grant or donation.

This feature is **not available to all collectives** and must follow specific conditions:

***

## Who can use “Request a Grant”?

* **Only projects hosted as Funds** (not standard Collectives)
* The applicant must be a **nonprofit or equivalent structure** (e.g. foundation, ASBL, charity, NGO)
* Private individuals or informal collectives **cannot** use this option

***

## Requirements for submitting a Grant Request

When a nonprofit uses the “Request a Grant” feature, they must include:

1. **A copy of their legal bylaws** (*statuts*)
2. **A signed letter** officially requesting the grant, outlining:
   * The purpose and objectives of the requested funding
   * How the funds will be used in alignment with the fund’s mission
   * The legal name and contact details of the nonprofit organization
3. **A bank account holder statement of the nonprofit**

> These documents help us assess legal eligibility, ensure compliance with funder requirements, and prepare reporting if needed.

***

## Internal review process

All grant requests are reviewed manually by the OSE team.\
If accepted, the funds are transferred directly to the nonprofit's official bank account, and the transaction is recorded transparently on the fund page.

For any questions about this feature, contact the finance or legal coordinator.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# The Partnership

## Legal Relationship: Indirect Representation

The relationship between your Collective and Open Source Europe (OSE) is one of **indirect representation** (*représentation indirecte* / *middellijke vertegenwoordiging*).

This means:

* Your Collective remains fully responsible for its own activities, including legal and tax compliance.
* OSE acts as a fiscal host and intermediary, not as the legal representative or owner of your funds or operations.

> **Important**: Your Collective **must not** use OSE's tax identification number (e.g. VAT number) for invoicing or registration purposes. If you need a tax number, you are responsible for obtaining your own in accordance with local law.

***

## Invoicing Guidelines

To stay compliant with our hosting terms:

* Invoices must be addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number to have invoices issued.
* Third parties must treat your Collective as an unincorporated group or individual for VAT purposes.
* If VAT does not apply, the invoice must cite the relevant VAT exemption article.

> **Danger:** If an invoice is wrongly addressed to OSE, it must be canceled and replaced. Repeated errors may lead to the end of your fiscal hosting agreement.

***

## Donations from Your Collective

Ordinary external donations may be made to identified nonprofit organisations after OSE has reviewed and approved the beneficiary, purpose and funding conditions. Contact OSE before committing or requesting payment. Other recipient types require a specific assessment, without any promise of acceptance.

Before passing on funds received under a grant agreement or for a restricted purpose, OSE checks whether the transfer is permitted and which obligations continue to apply. Any required funder approval must be obtained. A transfer does not automatically release OSE from its responsibilities under the original funding agreement.

After OSE has approved the arrangement:

1. Ask the recipient to submit an expense via your Collective's page.
2. Include:
   * A **signed letter** from the beneficiary confirming the purpose and amount.
   * A **copy of their incorporation document**.
   * Their **bank identification document**.

> **Danger:** The ordinary external donation route is for identified nonprofit organisations. Other cases require specific assessment and are not automatically accepted. A payment in exchange for goods, services or visibility is not treated as an ordinary donation; contact OSE before making that commitment.

***

## VAT & Nonprofit Status

Collectives hosted by OSE are not legal entities and **must pay VAT** on purchases:

* VAT must be listed on invoices (unless an exemption applies).
* The **reverse charge mechanism does not apply** to Collectives — only registered businesses can use it.

> **Note:** [Read more: VAT in Europe and how it works in OSE](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/the-partnership/vat-in-europe-and-how-it-works-in-ose/)

***

## Questions?

Email us any time at <home@opensourceeurope.org>. We're happy to help!


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# VAT in Europe and How It Works in OSE

## General Principles

Collectives hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE) are unincorporated initiatives primarily funded through donations. As such, they are **not eligible for VAT refunds** and must **always pay VAT** on goods and services purchased.

VAT (Value Added Tax) is a general consumption tax that applies to most goods and services within the European Union. Even if your Collective is not a registered entity, VAT is still due on your expenses.

> **Note:** Learn more: [VAT explained – European Commission](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/taxation-1/value-added-tax-vat_en)

***

## VAT Within the Same Country

Invoices issued within your country (e.g. Belgium) must include VAT unless the supplier is legally exempt.

OCE itself is **not VAT-exempt**, so if it issues an invoice (e.g. for services), VAT will be applied based on the applicable Belgian rate.

> **Note:** Belgian VAT details: [Finance Belgium](https://finance.belgium.be/en)

***

## Cross-Border VAT and Reverse Charge

The **reverse charge mechanism** lets VAT-registered businesses handle cross-border VAT internally (by declaring both output and input VAT).

However, this mechanism **only applies between two VAT-registered businesses**. Because OCE-hosted Collectives are **not legal entities**, they cannot apply the reverse charge mechanism.

> **Danger:** This means you **must pay VAT** on cross-border invoices from EU-based suppliers — just like any individual or unregistered group.

> **Note:** Learn more: [EU VAT rules – Your Europe](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/taxation/vat/vat-rules-rates/index_en.htm)

***

## Summary

* Collectives **must pay VAT** on all eligible purchases, whether national or cross-border.
* **Reverse charge rules do not apply**.
* If an invoice omits VAT but you are not VAT-registered, ask the vendor to correct it — or justify the exemption clearly.

***

## Questions?

Still unsure about VAT or invoicing rules? Email us at <home@opensourceeurope.org> — we're happy to help!


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Applying for Grants

Use this guide when a funder may support your Collective through OSE. Your Collective leads the application and project; OSE reviews its own role and commitments.

## The grant journey

1. **Before submitting:** check the funder's requirements and contact OSE. If the application names OSE as recipient or signatory, OSE must review and accept that role before submission.
2. **If awarded:** share the grant agreement and arrange the necessary agreements and payment instructions with OSE.
3. **When funds arrive:** use the Collective budget in line with the funding conditions. A promised grant is not an available balance.
4. **During the project:** prepare activity reports and project monitoring. OSE provides accounting information it holds and validates what engages OSE.

The detailed agreement, communication and reporting requirements follow below. See also [hosting fees](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost) and [spending the grant budget](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/).

## Overview

Open Source Europe (OSE) enables hosted Collectives to receive grants from institutional and philanthropic funders, both in Europe and internationally. Our team helps you prepare the arrangements for receiving and managing the grant.

> **Important**: If a grant application names OSE as recipient or signatory, contact OSE **before submission** so the team can review and accept its role and commitments.

***

## Initial Steps

1. **Contact OSE early**

   Email <home@opensourceeurope.org> to let us know about the grant opportunity. We'll help assess whether it's compatible with fiscal hosting through OSE.
2. **Check funder requirements**

   Not all funders allow grants to be awarded to fiscally sponsored initiatives. Be sure to confirm with them whether a hosted structure is accepted.
3. **For U.S. funders**

   Contact the OSE team to arrange the documentation required by your funder. See [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

***

## Grant Agreements & Receiving Funds

1. **Grant Agreement**

   The funder will provide a grant agreement. This must be signed by the confirmed recipient entity.\
   Please share the agreement with us via <home@opensourceeurope.org>, or have the funder reach out to us directly.
2. **Mandate Agreement**

   Your initiative will also need to sign a Mandate Agreement with OSE.\
   This formalizes the arrangement and must be signed by two members of your initiative.
3. **Bank Transfer**

   The OSE team will provide the appropriate bank transfer instructions for the agreed grant arrangement.
4. **Allocation on the Platform**

   Once the grant is received, the funds will appear on your Collective’s Open Collective page as available balance.

***

## Funder Communication

* **Acknowledgments**

  You can publicly recognize funders on your Collective page. Their name will appear in your list of contributors unless they choose to remain anonymous.
* **Updates**

  Keep your funders informed by posting regular updates through the Open Collective platform.
* **Ongoing Communication**

  Any requests or messages from funders sent to OSE will be forwarded to your initiative for follow-up.

***

## Grant Reporting

The Collective prepares activity reports and project monitoring. OSE provides the accounting information it holds and validates statements or commitments that engage OSE. Follow the reporting requirements and deadlines of the grant agreement.

***

## Need Help?

The Collective leads its own fundraising. OSE may occasionally share opportunities or make introductions, according to its capacity; it does not promise a structured fundraising service or funding success. For questions about receiving and administering a grant, contact <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

## Hosting fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost).

# Contributions in cryptocurrencies

OSE Collectives can receive cryptocurrency donations through the established route:

**Every.org → Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE → the Collective’s budget on Open Collective.**

## Set up the donation page

Contact OSE first at <home@opensourceeurope.org>. The team creates and hosts an Every.org page for your Collective and provides the applicable instructions, documents, fees and transfer information. Every.org is the required starting point for this cryptocurrency route.

## Receive and transfer funds

Cryptocurrency is converted into conventional currency before it is allocated to the Collective. OSE does not pay cryptocurrency out to the Collective.

The Collective may ask OSE at any time to transfer the funds received on Every.org to its Open Collective budget. The team handles the intermediary steps. A request at any time does not mean an immediate payout; no fixed twice-yearly transfer schedule applies.

## Fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost). Contact OSE for the applicable processing, conversion and intermediary costs before sending funds. Do not assume a combined fee or transfer date.

More ways to raise funds

Open Collective includes crowdfunding tools and is the usual way to raise funds for an OSE Collective.

## External platforms

External platforms such as Patreon, Ko-fi and GoFundMe are considered case by case. Contact OSE before configuring a campaign to receive funds through OSE. The team checks payout arrangements, available records and any promised benefits before confirming whether the setup can be accepted. Do not assume that choosing an organisation with a similar name will route donations to your OSE Collective.

## Fundraising support

The Collective leads its fundraising. OSE may occasionally share opportunities or make introductions, according to its capacity, without guaranteeing funding or providing a standard fundraising service.

For an unidentified incoming payment, [contact OSE](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/) with its reference so the team can investigate its allocation. This is distinct from the handling of inactive Collectives’ balances.

## Why Donate via Open Source Europe?

Open Source Europe (OSE) enables donors to support impactful Collectives transparently and securely. Hosted Collectives don't need their own bank account or legal entity — OSE receives and manages funds on their behalf. Donors can also choose to be publicly acknowledged on the Collective’s profile.

***

## Accepted Payment Methods

You can make a contribution through:

* **Credit or Debit Card**
* **PayPal**
* **Bank Transfer** (SEPA or international)

> **Note**: When making a bank transfer, please include the name of the Collective and your order number in the payment reference. If not possible, contact us at <home@opensourceeurope.org> with your transaction details to ensure proper attribution.

***

## Information Required

When donating, you may be asked for:

* Your **full name**
* Your **email address**
* Your **organization name** (if applicable)
* Your **payment method details**

# Refunds

Can I refund a donation or get a refund for one I have made?

## Can I request a refund for a donation?

Yes, under certain conditions. Open Source Europe (OSE) can process refunds for contributions made via credit card, bank transfer, or PayPal.

### Refund Timeframes

* **Credit Card or Bank Transfer**: Refunds can be requested within **90 days** of the contribution date.
* **PayPal**: Refunds can be requested within **60 days** of the contribution date.

> **Important**: Refunds are only issued to the original payment method. For card payments processed through Stripe, Stripe and the card issuer handle the routing of the refund, including where the original card has expired or been replaced. OSE reviews the request and initiates an approved refund; it does not control the bank's handling of the funds.

***

## How to Request a Refund

Contact the Collective administrators first; they forward your request to OSE. If the administrators do not respond, contact OSE directly at <home@opensourceeurope.org>. A request does not guarantee a refund. Include the following details:

* **URL of the donation** (e.g., `https://opencollective.com/europe/contributions/528520`)
* **Date and amount** of the transaction
* **Reason** for the refund request

> **Note**: After reviewing the request, OSE may decline a refund if the contribution was authorized and the funds have already been used to support the Collective's activities.

***

## Refund Processing Times

OSE first reviews the refund request. If approved, OSE initiates the refund. The time it takes for the funds to reach you then depends on the payment method, payment provider and bank. No fixed processing or receipt date is guaranteed.

These processing steps are separate from the request deadlines above: 90 days for card or bank-transfer contributions and 60 days for PayPal.

***

## Additional Information

* Refunds are only processed to the **original payment method**.
* The handling of an expired card or closed account depends on the payment provider and bank; it is not an automatic reason for OSE to declare a refund impossible.
* For contributions made via **manual bank transfer**, the administrators forward the request to OSE to discuss refund options; contact OSE directly if they do not respond.

***

## Need Assistance?

For any questions or further assistance regarding refunds, please contact us at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Setting up GitHub Sponsors

Guide to connecting GitHub Sponsors for Organizations to your Collective

## Choose your starting point

* **New organisation profile:** follow First activation. Have your OSE-hosted Collective URL ready and use an organisation owner account with two-factor authentication.
* **Already sponsored through another host:** start with Already using GitHub Sponsors?. Moving on Open Collective does not move your Sponsors setup automatically.
* **Personal GitHub account:** discuss the arrangement with OSE; the activation steps below are for organisations.

**Expected outcome:** a project Sponsors profile using OSE's fiscal-host route, subject to GitHub review. If the host label or payout setup is unclear, contact OSE before continuing.

Use GitHub Sponsors for your project with OSE as fiscal host and your Collective on Open Collective as the destination for its budget.

## First activation for a GitHub organisation

1. Your project needs a Collective hosted by OSE. The person configuring Sponsors must be an owner of the project’s GitHub organisation and have two-factor authentication enabled.
2. Visit [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors), choose **Get sponsored**, and select the project’s own GitHub organisation.
3. Select **This organization is using a fiscal host**, then select the host entry corresponding to OSE. If the label is unclear, contact OSE before continuing. The public GitHub guide may still show an earlier name.
4. In **Fiscal host project profile URL**, enter your Collective’s Open Collective URL, for example `https://opencollective.com/your-project`. Do not enter OSE’s GitHub organisation URL in this field.
5. Complete the project profile and request GitHub approval. Activation depends on GitHub’s review; no approval deadline is promised.

OSE’s GitHub organisation is [opensourceeurope](https://github.com/opensourceeurope). You configure sponsorship for your own project through the fiscal-host route; do not set up your own Stripe account for that route. If you encounter an unexpected payout setup step, contact OSE.

GitHub also supports personal sponsored accounts. This guide describes organisation setup; discuss a personal-account case with OSE.

## Already using GitHub Sponsors?

Contact OSE to organise a change from another fiscal host. Moving your Collective on Open Collective does **not** automatically update its GitHub Sponsors host. OSE accompanies the process and coordinates with GitHub where necessary. Do not assume the migration is complete until the GitHub setup has been confirmed.

## Fees and sponsorship benefits

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost). GitHub’s own fees are separate; consult its [current fee guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/sponsoring-open-source-contributors/about-sponsorships-fees-and-taxes).

If you plan to promise goods, services or other benefits to sponsors, contact OSE before commitment or receipt of payment. GitHub’s tier features do not automatically make an arrangement acceptable to OSE.

## Official instructions

* [Using a fiscal host](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/receiving-sponsorships-through-github-sponsors/using-a-fiscal-host-to-receive-github-sponsors-payouts)
* [Setting up Sponsors for an organisation](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/receiving-sponsorships-through-github-sponsors/setting-up-github-sponsors-for-your-organization)

Questions: <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

# Wire Transfer Instructions via Open Collective Platform

Please note that all funds have this option available.

## Overview

If you prefer to contribute to a Collective via bank transfer, Open Source Europe (OSE) provides a straightforward process to facilitate this.

***

## Step-by-Step Guide

1. **Initiate the Donation Process**
   * Navigate to the Collective's page you wish to support.
   * Click on the **“Contribute”** button.
   * Select **“Bank Transfer”** as your payment method.
2. **Receive Transfer Instructions**
   * After confirming your contribution, you'll receive an email containing:
     * OSE's bank account details.
     * A unique **Order Number** associated with your contribution.
3. **Complete the Bank Transfer**
   * Initiate the transfer from your bank, ensuring you:
     * Use the **exact bank details** provided.
     * Include the **Order Number** and the **Collective's name** in the payment reference.

> **Important**: Omitting the Order Number or Collective's name may delay the allocation of your funds.

1. **Processing Time**
   * Allow **up to seven business days from the date you send the bank transfer** for the contribution to appear in the Collective's budget. This is an indicative timeframe, not a guarantee. If it has not appeared after this period, contact OSE using the details below.
   * Once the hosting team has confirmed receipt and allocated the transfer to your Collective, the contribution will appear in its budget.

***

## Visual Guide

[Image removed: The Open Collective thank-you page after a contribution, with a pending notice and payment instructions that give the amount, IBAN, BIC and order reference for the bank transfer]

[Image removed: The confirmation email, with the bank transfer instructions: amount, IBAN, BIC, order reference and recipient address]

*Example of the confirmation screen displaying bank transfer details.*

***

## Troubleshooting

* **Didn't Receive the Instruction Email?**
  * Check your spam or junk folder.
  * If not found, contact us at <home@opensourceeurope.org>
* **Funds Not Reflected After Seven Business Days from Sending?**

  * Ensure the payment reference included the correct Order Number and Collective's name.
  * Provide us with:
    * The **transaction receipt**.
    * The **amount sent**.
    * The **date of transfer**.
    * The **sender's name**.

  Send this information to <home@opensourceeurope.org> for assistance.

## Hosting fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost).

# Open Source Europe documentation

Practical guidance for joining OSE, receiving funds and managing your Collective.

**New to OSE?** [Start your application](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/). **Already accepted?** [Follow your first steps](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/basics/).

## Choose your task

- [Join OSE](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/): Check whether hosting fits your project and prepare your application.
- [Run your Collective](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/basics/): Start after acceptance, manage your budget and keep your contacts up to date.
- [Receive funds](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/): Choose a donation route, receive a grant or connect GitHub Sponsors.
- [Pay and get reimbursed](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/): Choose an invoice or reimbursement and prepare your payment request.
- [Fees and hosting rules](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/): Understand hosting costs and find answers about your arrangement with OSE.
- [Get help](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/): Find the right contact for a question, a payment issue or a sensitive concern.

## Understand OSE

Read [what OSE offers](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/), explore [budget decisions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/guides/deciding-on-how-to-use-your-money/), or consult the [payment FAQ](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/expenses-and-getting-paid-faqs/).

For a safeguarding concern, go directly to the [safeguarding policy and contacts](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/safeguarding-policy/).

Open Source Europe is a Belgian Association (ASBL/vzw) with a tech platform that enables over 400 open source groups to raise and spend more than 1 million euros annually, all in full transparency.

### Our Mission

We support movements and decentralized communities by providing the infrastructure necessary to:

* Facilitate the launch of new projects.
* Manage and oversee financial operations.
* Ensure legal and fiscal compliance for open source initiatives.

If you are an open-source project, OSE is here to help you achieve your goals by removing the administrative burden of fund management.

Additionally, we collaborate with foundations and philanthropists to establish dedicated funds, enabling them to re-grant resources to open source initiatives globally.

***

### How We Can Help

#### For Open Source Collectives

By partnering with OSE, your group can:

* Launch and manage projects effectively without the need to incorporate a separate legal entity.
* Streamline financial operations using the Open Collective platform.
* Connect with global philanthropic opportunities and corporate sponsors.

#### For Foundations and Philanthropists

We offer professional assistance in:

* Creating and managing philanthropic funds.
* Facilitating transparent re-granting processes.
* Supporting open source initiatives on a global scale through a recognized European structure.

***

### Get Started

* [Apply for hosting](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
* [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/Na7BpVcm)
* [Contact us](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org)

# Terms of Service

## Hosting agreement

Hosting with Open Source Europe is governed by the association's Terms of Hosting.

The [Terms of Hosting for the association](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15Wkvfn5ou-is_eUjautjDv4JZ-tiY2-c/edit) are the reference document for this hosting relationship. [Contact the team](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org) to obtain the applicable version and any additional agreement relevant to your project.

## Main responsibilities

This overview explains the main points of the association's Terms of Hosting. It does not replace or amend the agreement.

* Your initiative remains responsible for its activities and related obligations. Hosting does not make the initiative a legal extension of the association.
* The association receives and administers funds on the initiative's behalf through an indirect representation relationship.
* The initiative retains its intellectual property unless a separate agreement provides otherwise.
* The initiative cannot bind the association to an agreement with a third party without prior written approval.
* Contributions and expenses must be recorded transparently on the platform. Expense requests require supporting documents and review.
* Funds must support the initiative's stated purpose. The initiative must keep its description up to date and publish updates at least annually.
* Administrative fees and directly related processing expenses are deducted according to the applicable agreement.

## Starting, changing or ending the arrangement

Contact the team before entering into grant agreements, making commitments on behalf of the association, or changing your project's activities.

The Terms of Hosting provide for termination with **30 days' written notice**. Valid outstanding expenses and any remaining balance are handled under the agreement's termination provisions. A remaining balance is not automatically available for distribution to individual administrators.

For current guidance on contributions, see [Contributions FAQ](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/contributions-faq/). If your planned activity raises a question about the scope of the hosting agreement, contact the team before proceeding.

## Contact

<home@opensourceeurope.org>


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Equivalency Determination Certificate

## Grants from U.S. foundations

Open Source Europe helps hosted projects receive grants from U.S. foundations through an Equivalency Determination (ED) arrangement.

Contact the OSE team before applying. We coordinate with the funder, provide the relevant documentation and arrange for the grant to reach your project.

## Preparing a grant application

Contact <home@opensourceeurope.org> early, with:

* The funder's name and the project to be supported.
* The proposed amount, purpose and application deadline.
* Any eligibility requirements or draft grant agreement.

The team will provide the current ED documentation and confirm the details to use in the grant agreement. An ED does not guarantee that a particular funder or grant programme will accept an application.

## Donations from individuals

An ED is distinct from the route for U.S. tax-deductible donations through Myriad USA. See [Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/).

## Documentation for the funder

The ED used for this arrangement is held by Open Collective Europe Foundation. Where this route is used, it receives the grant and transfers it to OSE for your project. The OSE team coordinates these steps.

# What We Offer

Open Source Europe provides the legal and financial infrastructure that open source projects need to thrive. Our services are designed to let you focus on your code, not on paperwork.

We offer one core service: **fiscal hosting**, which bundles everything you need to operate professionally.

***

## Core Infrastructure

### A Legal Home for Your Project

Operate under our Belgian non-profit association (ASBL/vzw). This allows your project to receive funds, manage contracts, and act as a single legal entity without the complexity and overhead of creating your own.

### Transparent Financial Tools

Use the Open Collective platform to manage your budget, receive donations, and pay contributors and expenses with full transparency. Your community and backers can see every transaction in real-time, building trust and accountability.

### Access to Grants and Funding

Many foundations and companies want to fund the open source ecosystem but find it difficult to support unincorporated groups. We act as a trusted intermediary, making your project eligible to receive grants from these larger institutional funders.

***

## Why Choose Fiscal Hosting?

This structure is ideal for open source projects seeking to focus on their mission without the administrative burden of formal incorporation. It provides:

* **Instant Legitimacy:** High-level compliance for corporate sponsors.
* **Reduced Overhead:** No need for dedicated accounting or legal teams.
* **Collective Power:** Join an ecosystem of over 400 projects sharing the same robust infrastructure.

***

## Get Started

Ready to join a supportive community of open source projects building the future of software?

* [Apply for hosting](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
* [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/Na7BpVcm)
* [Contact the team](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org)

# Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors

## An established route for U.S. giving

U.S. individuals and businesses can support OSE Collectives through **Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE**. This established arrangement enables U.S. tax-deductible donations within the limits of applicable tax rules. The donor’s actual deduction depends on their circumstances.

## Choose the appropriate donation route

Contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org> before payment with the name of the Collective to support. The team organises the route, reference, documents, applicable costs and transfer arrangements.

* **Regular fundraising from U.S. donors:** an Every.org page organised with OSE is the preferred option. Funds follow Every.org → Myriad → OCEF → OSE.
* **A larger donation:** the donor gives directly to Myriad, without Every.org, then funds follow Myriad → OCEF → OSE. Ask the team for the correct instructions; no universal amount threshold is specified here.

A donation through the ordinary Open Collective checkout does not automatically use this arrangement. Confirm which organisation will issue the donation documentation for the selected route.

The [current OSE hosting fees](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost) apply. The team will confirm any additional costs associated with the route.

## Other cases

If the tax-deductible route for your circumstances has not already been confirmed, contact OSE before giving to check the available route and documents. OSE does not guarantee an individual tax benefit.

Cryptocurrency donations have a specific mandatory Every.org starting point: see [Cryptocurrency contributions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/contributions-in-cryptocurrencies/).

For grants from U.S. foundations, see [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

Further information: [Myriad FAQ](https://myriadusa.org/about/faqs/) and [ways to give](https://myriadusa.org/waystogive/).


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# The Open Collective Platform

A shared tool for managing contributions, expenses, and grants with full transparency.

## A transparent financial and community management tool

Open Collective is a digital platform that enables hosted initiatives and philanthropic partners to raise, manage, and distribute funds with full transparency. Each group or fund hosted by Open Source Europe receives its own public page, equipped with tools to:

* Collect financial contributions: Accept donations via credit card, PayPal, or bank transfer, and manage grants.
* Manage expenses and disbursements: Submit, approve, and reimburse expenses directly through the platform.
* Display a transparent budget: All income and expenditures are visible in real-time, enhancing trust and accountability.
* Engage with the community: Post updates, host events, and share progress with supporters.

This integrated approach simplifies financial administration and fosters a collaborative environment for your initiative or fund.

## Support for Philanthropic Regranting

Beyond grassroots initiatives, the platform is also a powerful tool for foundations and funders. Through Open Collective, OSE can set up dedicated online funds to:

* Receive donations or grants earmarked for specific causes or regions
* Disburse grants to multiple projects (including informal or unincorporated groups) in a streamlined, transparent manner
* Enable funders and the public to track how resources are used

Each fund has its own profile page, budget, and update feed, just like a Collective. This makes it easy for regranting partners to communicate their goals, track disbursements, and meet reporting obligations with minimal overhead.

## Why transparency matters

Transparency is a cornerstone of the Open Collective platform. By making financial information publicly accessible, initiatives and funders can:

* Build credibility: Demonstrate responsible fund management to donors and stakeholders
* Simplify reporting: Funders can directly monitor how their resources are allocated
* Enhance collaboration: Encourage trust and coordination between grantees and grantmakers

Financial transactions are public, but personal details like names and email addresses are only visible to authorized admins.

## Key Features

* Real-time budget tracking
* Integrated expense and payout tools
* Custom donation tiers and fundraising campaigns
* Event management tools
* Automated monthly financial summaries
* Public updates and communication channels


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Umbrella organisation

Open Source Europe (OSE) provides a shared legal and financial framework for open source projects, developer networks, and software communities.

## Collective Infrastructure

As an umbrella organisation, OSE acts as the fiscal host for over 400 initiatives. Each project operates independently on the Open Collective platform with its own public page and transparent budget, while benefiting from the legal standing of a professional Belgian non-profit (ASBL/vzw).

This structure allows communities to manage funds, pay service providers on compliant invoices, and receive grants without the overhead of maintaining their own legal entity.

***

## Key Benefits

* **Simplified Legal Framework:** Skip the complexity of non-profit incorporation, bank account openings, and statutory bookkeeping.
* **Grant Eligibility:** Access funding from foundations, corporations, and public authorities that require a registered non-profit intermediary.
* **Professional Back-office:** We handle the administrative heavy lifting, including expense processing, bookkeeping, and annual financial reporting.
* **Radical Transparency:** Every transaction is logged in real-time, building immediate trust with your backers and contributors.
* **Ecosystem Access:** Join a network of like-minded maintainers and projects within the European open source landscape.

***

> **Tip:** ## Responsibilities and Alignment
>
> To maintain the integrity of the umbrella, hosted projects must adhere to three core principles:
>
> 1. **Mission Alignment:** Projects must actively support the development or sustainability of open source software.
> 2. **Non-Profit Compliance:** As an ASBL/vzw, projects must operate within the limits of Belgian law, focusing on community benefit rather than purely commercial for-profit activities.
> 3. **Operational Transparency:** All financial activities must be conducted through the Open Collective platform to ensure public accountability.

***

## Use Cases We Support

* **Open Source Libraries:** A legal home for critical libraries to receive corporate and individual donations.
* **Project Ecosystems:** A unified structure for a suite of related tools managed by a distributed community.
* **Tech Communities:** Regional developer groups or meetups managing funds for events, travel stipends, and venues.

***

[Apply to join the umbrella](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
